name: Production liveness review in the goal runner
description: The runner's liveness check: it first detects a usage limit from the session file, skips the model when a subagent is in flight, then sends the review prompt with elapsed time, idle time and log tail to a one-shot command-line model call and parses the verdict. Any failure to reach or read the reviewer means keep running.
advantages: Judges the situation rather than matching words, and fails open so work is protected.
disadvantages: Each review costs a model call and depends on the command-line tool being present, and its judgement can vary between runs.

name: Live model reviewer arm
description: Fills the production review prompt exactly as the runner does, sends it through the same one-shot call and reads it with the production parser, scored against hand-labelled logs. It needs the command-line tool and a small call per log.
advantages: Measures the shipped reviewer itself, including its prompt and parser, with false stops counted separately. Selected because: core/goal_runner.py SubprocessGoalRunner._review_liveness (the review prompt and parser, run through claude -p at the review model)
disadvantages: Costs model calls, cannot run where the tool is absent, and the labelled set is small without held-out real-run logs.

name: Keyword and threshold rule floor
description: A baseline decides from fixed signals: stop on a named usage or credit limit, on text saying the worker is blocked on a person, on the same command repeated, or on a long idle with no sign of a machine at work. Everything else keeps running.
advantages: Free, instant and explainable, and a fair floor a model reviewer must match.
disadvantages: Written with the cases in view, so its score is optimistic, and keyword lists miss new phrasings and cannot read an unfamiliar log. Idle thresholds are blunt.

name: Production judges under a scripted provider
description: Calls the real overseer, reach-judge parser and block builder, quest ranker and sufficiency helpers with a scripted provider that returns fixed output or raises, so only the deterministic halves are exercised.
advantages: Fast, free and exact on the parts that must never fail, with failure injection. Selected because: core/reach_judge.py, core/quest_judge.py, core/overseer.py, core/sufficiency.py wired by core/orchestrator_judges.py
disadvantages: Compared against a trusting baseline only, and it says nothing about what the real models decide.

name: Production guard engines under test
description: Calls the real link guard with a fake fetch table, link extraction, an in-memory recipe store and the pure anticipation functions directly, with no model or network.
advantages: Deterministic and fast, and covers all three guards with the real code. Selected because: core/link_guard.py (build_link_guard), core/recipes.py, core/anticipation.py wired by config
disadvantages: Does not show live behaviour of replay through a real model or real network noise, which other solutions own.

name: Eligibility gate mixin
description: Methods on the autopilot pass that test, in order, daily budget, cadence in the quest's zone, Run now, reactive trigger, roster day and backpressure, and read open asks, so a quest is skipped with a reason before any goal is read.
advantages: Cheap, ordered and explainable gates that follow the person's settings exactly.
disadvantages: The ordering and interplay of many rules is intricate, and a new setting needs a matching case.

name: Scripted-client gate evaluation arm
description: Runs the production autopilot pass for one quest against a client that answers only what a gate reads and a pinned clock, recording anything reached past the gates, so the outcome is exactly a skip reason or passage.
advantages: Tests the real gates deterministically with no model calls. Selected because: runner/autopilot_gates.py GatesMixin._gate_quest, the budget check in AutopilotPass.run and the pure predicates in runner/autopilot_periods.py
disadvantages: Measures only the decision to run, not the work after it.

name: Prompts without the intent frame
description: Quest-scoped prompts carry the quest alone: its outcome, current state and preferences, with no mention of the intent it serves.
advantages: Zero added tokens and nothing to go wrong. Selected because: Nothing is measured yet: the frame ships behind no switch because it costs nothing for people without intents, and the no-frame arm stays selected until the metric decides
disadvantages: Choices and judgments ignore the person's top intents, and gaps under an intent go unnoticed.

name: Computed frame in the prompt
description: The server computes a short frame from stored ids and the autopilot brief, the chat quest facts and the quest card carry it; no model call.
advantages: Cheap, deterministic, and empty for people without intents.
disadvantages: Gives the model only names and links; it cannot answer detailed questions about the specification without a drill-down.

name: Frame plus intent card and record drill-down
description: The frame, one context card per top intent chosen by relevance, and a get_spec read that returns the best-matching records for a question.
advantages: Answers questions about the specification by meaning and pays tokens only for what a turn uses.
disadvantages: More moving parts; the card must be kept in step with the intent and the drill-down must rank records well.

name: Frame plus a lazily generated quest specification
description: The frame plus one model-written specification of a ready quest, generated the first time an AI consumer needs it, reachable through the drill-down.
advantages: Adds what the quest's own fields cannot say: dimension ideals, links and sufficiency gaps.
disadvantages: One model call per used quest and a risk of restating fields the quest already holds.

name: Generic method in the standing instructions
description: Every deep run carries the same principles as required standing instructions, whatever the task serves.
advantages: Carries the author's principles into every run with nothing to build.
disadvantages: Large, and says nothing about the problem, ideal or metric the task serves.

name: Slice of the specification before the task
description: The brief gets the slice for the quest or solution the task serves, with the standing instructions kept short.
advantages: Specific to the task and small.
disadvantages: Needs a source for the slice for each kind of specification; built for a repository's ESOI records only.

name: Slice before and write-back after
description: The slice before the task, and the runner reads the metric before and after the work and writes the readings to the run's metric ledger, beside any result the worker records. The readings go to a per-run file of readings in a temporary folder (the metric ledger of docs/explanation/metric-results.md, core/metric_results.py) and onto the task report; a card's usage_count and last_outcome are set by FileContextStore.record from the kind of turn.
advantages: Closes the loop so the next task starts from what this one learned. Selected because: Joshua directed on 2026-10-21 that every run's metric result before and after is recorded by code; the replay metric (task_replay) is not built, so this is a direction, not a measured win.
disadvantages: Needs the measured replay to confirm it helps. Readings expire with the temporary folder and never reach the record; nothing says what moved; nothing makes a run fix a record it found wrong; a card's outcome is not tied to any metric.

name: Lexical TF-IDF, optional vector search, parallel batched model judging
description: Field-weighted TF-IDF over the index's own terms proposes candidates; an injected vector search proposes more, fused by reciprocal rank; the candidates' one-line descriptions are cut into batches and a cheap model judges all batches in parallel; ids not offered are dropped, a failed batch keeps its candidates, and each selected record brings its links.
advantages: Words, meaning and judgement each do what they are good at; latency is one call; degrades to the lexical candidates when a model or vector call fails.
disadvantages: Costs one cheap model call per batch of candidates; the vector search is the consumer's to supply.

name: Lexical top few only
description: The best few lexical matches and their links, with no vector search and no model.
advantages: Free and instant; the baseline for what the rest adds.
disadvantages: Misses a record that shares no word with the request, and cannot tell a keyword match that does not apply.

name: Lexical vector gated
description: Lexical plus vector candidates, then a confidence gate: a clear case is answered from the two searches' agreement and an empty case returns nothing, both with no model call; every other request costs one call that judges the best ``GATE_POOL`` candidates together. Cheaper and faster than judging every request in batches, with the model kept for the requests that need it. With no provider the ambiguous requests return the best fused candidates.
advantages: One model call (or none) per request instead of one per batch: a clear case and an empty case are answered from the two searches alone, so it is cheaper and faster than judging every request. Selected because: the 2026-10-20 run of metric-spec-selection on the labelled requests (the results log has the commit and the cases) ranked lexical-vector-gated first on the balanced score, above lexical-vector-llm (which returned a crowd), lexical-vector and lexical-only
disadvantages: The gate thresholds are tuned on this dataset and can answer a clear-looking wrong case without a model's check; needs a vector search that returns scores.

name: Slice before and write-back onto each record (planned)
description: Planned. The slice before the task as in slice-and-writeback; after it, the run's readings are appended to the results log with the run and the solution. A record the run found wrong or missing is edited directly in the same commit as the work, with the reason in the commit message, and the record's row in esoi/tracker/ (the review files esoi tracker build writes, one row per record) gets its tracking columns updated: last run in tracking_updated, outcome in tracking_status, movement, what moved and the reason for any change in tracking_notes. A card gets the same in usage_count, last_outcome and provenance. Only a change to the owner's own words (an intent's vision statement, the ideals the owner wrote) is raised as a proposal, and only the escalation triggers raise a decision request.
advantages: One source of truth per kind, no new file per run, specifications kept current by the runs that use them, and people asked only when a change needs them.
disadvantages: The tracking columns are filled by hand today, so a machine writer needs a lock for concurrent runs; a wrong edit is caught only by review of the history or by the metric; a run with no offline arm still has only a recorded reading.

name: Capped model draft per task (today)
description: A model drafts a metric from the task, bounded by a maximum number of calls per task.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: Ask the owner to write it (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. No draft is made; the owner is asked for the metric.
advantages: No cost; the metric is the owner's own words.
disadvantages: Most tasks stay metric-less; not built.

name: No-call floor of the quest ranker and reach judge
description: The model call of each judge is dropped: the quest ranker falls back to the home quest and no reach verdict is stamped, so the planner plans as for a request inside the readable sources.
advantages: Free and exact; the ablation that shows what the calls buy on hand-labelled cases.
disadvantages: Says nothing about what the models decide.

name: Live quest ranker and reach judge on a small model
description: The shipped quest-ranking and reach-judge prompts with a small model behind them (claude -p, cheapest tier), over hand-labelled cases on synthetic quests.
advantages: Measures what the two judges decide, with per-call tokens, seconds and cost tagged by prompt id for justified_model_spend.
disadvantages: Small case set; the cheapest tier is not the deployment's configured tier for the reach judge.
